title: Introduce token-heatwave metrics and alert-fanout-controller
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add token-heatwave telemetry and alert-fanout-controller. New dashboard: Heatwave Explorer. Backwards-compatible; server-side metric names added. Recommend migrating alert rules to fanout-based handlers for high-cardinality tenants.
description:
Motivation and summary: This PR instruments a new family of 'token-heatwave' metrics to detect sustained, high-intensity token activity (short-term bursts that persist across small windows) and introduces an alert-fanout-controller that routes observability alerts through tenant-aware dampening and escalation policies. The goal is to reduce noisy pager churn from transient multi-tenant bursts while providing clear visibility for true production regressions.

What this changes (high level):
- New metrics: token_heatwave_score{tenant,route,region,model_variant} (float), token_heatwave_window_count{tenant} (int), token_heatwave_phase{stage} (label). These are emitted from the serving runtime's telemetry hook and the edge proxy sampler.
- Lightweight tracing spans: heatwave.marker spans are attached to representative traces when score > threshold to allow quick drilldown into kernel queue and kv-cache pressure.
- Alert fanout controller: a small orchestration component in observability pipeline that applies tenant SLA and recent-noise-history to decide whether to forward, delay, or aggregate alert notifications. It integrates with the existing alerting backend and supports per-tenant silencing, exponential backoff, and safe-pass-through for high-severity SLO breaches.
- Dashboard: Heatwave Explorer (Grafana) with per-tenant calendar heatmap, per-route timeline, and correlated trace links.
- Tests and docs: unit tests for the score calc, e2e smoke in dev cluster, and docs/observability/heatwave.md with runbook guidance.

Design notes:
- Heatwave score is a weighted combination of short-window token rate, consecutive-window persistence, and kernel-queue occupancy. We intentionally keep the score bounded [0,1] for easy thresholding.
- To avoid cardinality explosion, we roll up low-traffic tenants into a sample 'tenants:small' bucket for the dashboard while still emitting tenant-specific metrics at low frequency.
- Fanout controller follows a policy chain: SLA exemption -> severity mapping -> recent-noise suppression -> final dispatch. Policies are declarative (YAML) and hot-reloadable.

Checklist: 
- [x] Instrument runtime metrics (serving/runtime/heatwave_instrumentation.go)
- [x] Edge proxy sampler update (proxy/sampler/heatwave_sampler.rs)
- [x] Tracing span attachment and link creation (runtime/tracing/heatwave_span.cpp)
- [x] Fanout controller service and tests (observability/fanout_controller/*)
- [x] Grafana dashboard JSON and dashboard provisioning (dashboards/heatwave-explorer.json)
- [x] Dev cluster smoke test and runbook (docs/observability/heatwave.md)

Commits (summary):
- Add heatwave score calculation, config and unit tests
- Emit token_heatwave_score and window counters from runtime telemetry hook
- Attach heatwave.marker spans to sampled traces when score threshold crossed
- Implement fanout controller with policy engine and test harness
- Dashboard and runbook additions
- Fix: reduce label cardinality by introducing small-tenant rollup path

Files changed (high-level):
- serving/runtime/heatwave_instrumentation.go (new) - score calc, config parsing
- proxy/sampler/heatwave_sampler.rs (modified) - sampling heuristics on edge
- runtime/tracing/heatwave_span.cpp (modified) - span creation and attributes
- observability/fanout_controller/main.go (new) - service entry point and policy engine
- observability/fanout_controller/policy.yaml (new) - example tenant policies
- dashboards/heatwave-explorer.json (new) - Grafana dashboard JSON
- docs/observability/heatwave.md (new) - operational runbook and migration notes
- observability/tests/heatwave_integration_test.go (new) - e2e smoke
- observability/ci/provision_heatwave_test.sh (modified) - add test provisioning script

Review conversation (selected):
- Diego Morales (review): "Nice approach. A few questions: how does this interact with existing token-burst alerts? We should ensure we don't introduce a blind spot for billing anomalies."
- Maya Chen (author): "Good catch — fanout controller includes an SLA exemption list and a separate mapping for billing alerts which always bypasses suppression. I added a unit test to cover that mapping."
- Priya Nair (review): "Policy YAML looks flexible. Can we add a default off-ramp to degrade to 'notify' after N suppressed cycles?"
- Maya Chen: "Added exponential backoff + guaranteed notify after 6 suppression cycles (configurable). See policy.yaml and tests. Also added metrics for suppression_count per tenant for visibility."
- Ethan Park (review): "Edge sampler changes look fine, but we need to be conscious of additional CPU cost on proxies; did you benchmark?"
- Maya Chen: "Yes — ran a dev-cluster perf run (results summarized in CI) showing <2% p50 CPU delta for the sampler under synthetic load. I also added a feature flag to gate heatwave sampling for low-tier regions."

CI and testing:
- CI run 1: build (pass), unit tests (pass), integration smoke (fail: flaky test in test harness)
- CI run 2 (after fix): build (pass), unit tests (pass), integration smoke (pass), lint (pass)
- Observability perf bench: included as an artifact; heatwave sampler added ~1.2% p50 CPU in edge proxy under load profile A.

Operational considerations and migration: 
- Backwards compatibility: metric names are additive; no existing dashboards are renamed. Consumers can opt-in to per-tenant metrics via a config flag.
- Rollout: feature flagged on by default in staging; gradual rollout to prod with a 2-week canary. Fanout controller deployed as a stateless service behind observability cluster with rollout-based traffic mirroring during initial window.
- Monitoring: new alerts added to the observability repo to track fanout controller health, policy reload failures, and suppression_count anomalies.

Follow-ups (post-merge):
- Add tenant-level UI controls in Console to view/snooze heatwave suppression (ENG-2048).
- Experiment with per-route adaptive thresholds driven by historical prompt-shape (ML follow-up).

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals from Diego, Priya and Ethan. Hotfix for flaky test included in the squash commit.

Notes for oncall: See docs/observability/heatwave.md for runbook. If the fanout controller fails and suppression_count spikes, alerts will fall back to default passthrough; check the fanout_controller logs and policy reload metrics.

Attachments: links to CI artifacts and dashboard provisioning are included in the PR (ci/artifacts/319847/*).
notes_for_oncall: If suppression_count per tenant unexpectedly increases, check fanout_controller.policy_reload_success (0/1) and the suppression_count metric; fallback behavior is passthrough if the service is unhealthy.
test_plan: Unit tests for score calc + policy engine run. Integration smoke on dev cluster with synthetic multi-tenant load. Manual validation of dashboard links and trace correlation in staging.
